name: NumFOCUS, Inc.
subcategory: fiscal sponsor for open-source scientific computing projects
origin_detail: US 501(c)(3) public charity (EIN 45-4547709, Austin, TX; tax exemption granted September 2012) created by the scientific Python community; Travis Oliphant is described as a founder of NumFOCUS. It acts as the legal entity for its fiscally sponsored projects and runs educational programmes.
flagship_projects: Fiscal sponsorship of NumPy, SciPy, pandas, Matplotlib, scikit-learn, Julia, Astropy, conda-forge, PETSc, Cantera, PyBaMM and others (63 sponsored projects)
openness_notes: A neutral nonprofit home for OSI-licensed scientific software; projects keep their own technical governance.
latest_value_type: annual revenue, IRS Form 990, fiscal year ending Dec 2024 (expenses $11,090,430)
risk_events: Two consecutive operating deficits: FY2023 revenue $7.25M vs expenses $9.95M; FY2024 revenue $8.38M vs expenses $11.09M. Net assets fell from $11.50M (2022) to $5.67M (2024).

Project Jupyter, once the best-known scientific Python project, is not on NumFOCUS's current sponsored-project list; its donations are now handled by LF Charities under the Linux Foundation's Jupyter Foundation (Nov 2024).
robustness: Diversified across 63 sponsored projects, but its own finances depend on grants, corporate sponsorship and events, and reserves roughly halved in two years. Projects can leave for other fiscal hosts, as Jupyter's move to the Linux Foundation shows.
physical_science_relevance: Fiscal home for core physical-science and numerical libraries: NumPy, SciPy, Astropy, SunPy, yt, Cantera (combustion chemistry), PyBaMM (battery modelling), PETSc, FEniCS, MDAnalysis, TARDIS, Gammapy and others.
openness_effect_assessment: NumFOCUS turned volunteer scientific-Python projects into entities able to receive grants and donations; revenue rose from $4,690 (2012) to $9.3M (2022). The open model's weakness shows in 2023-2024: spending outran income while the stack it supports became foundational for AI and data science.
key_takeaway: NumFOCUS is the main US nonprofit sustaining the scientific Python stack, at about $8-11M a year, small relative to the commercial AI value built on NumPy, pandas and scikit-learn. Its 2023-2024 deficits and Jupyter's move to the Linux Foundation suggest that community fiscal sponsors are being outcompeted by better-funded corporate-backed foundations.
